description: Anchored scoring rubric for W1 pilot evaluations. Each dimension is scored 1-5: 1 materially fails, 2 has major gaps, 3 is a competent baseline, 4 is strong and specific, and 5 is exceptional with cited evidence. Numeric impressions without anchor citation are rejected.

scoring_scale.1: Materially fails the brief or requirement.
scoring_scale.2: Has major gaps in required evidence, specificity, or execution.
scoring_scale.3: Competent baseline: addresses the requirement without a strong, cited distinction.
scoring_scale.4: Strong and specific: concrete, brief-grounded, and supported by cited evidence.
scoring_scale.5: Exceptional: unusually precise and complete with cited evidence that materially improves implementation confidence.

universal_evidence_requirement.description: Every finding row must carry all five fields. A missing field is a material failure on the evidence dimension (score 1), regardless of other content.

anchors.1: Generic placeholder values or a restatement of the brief replaces a decision.
anchors.2: Some specific values appear, but key decisions remain generic or hedged.
anchors.3: Competent, brief-relevant decisions with some generic framing remaining.
anchors.4: Concrete, brief-specific values, ratios, or token roles support nearly every decision.
anchors.5: Every decision is traceable to a cited product constraint or observed artifact; no template residue remains.

dimensions.label: Evidence completeness (all 5 required fields present per finding)

anchors.1: A finding has no evidence fields, or status alone is a bare checkmark.
anchors.2: Several fields are missing or cannot be tied to an artifact.
anchors.3: Most findings include usable evidence fields, with some thin or missing provenance.
anchors.4: Every finding has status, reason, remediation, evidence, and provenance.
anchors.5: All fields are present and evidence is measured or directly cited with traceable provenance.

dimensions.label: Fail-closed behavior (does not pass ambiguous or missing evidence)

anchors.1: Passes ambiguous evidence or accepts an unsupported n/a.
anchors.2: Names uncertainty but still permits a material unchecked assumption.
anchors.3: Usually fails closed, with one weakly justified boundary.
anchors.4: Missing measurements and unsupported skips produce explicit failures.
anchors.5: Every ambiguity is isolated, evidenced, and routed without inference; all n/a rows name a genuinely absent subject.

dimensions.label: Handoff fields — downstream skill can consume without re-deriving

anchors.1: No handoff exists, or it is a placeholder.
anchors.2: Handoff exists but leaves major values for downstream re-derivation.
anchors.3: A downstream worker can proceed, but some evidence references are thin.
anchors.4: All required handoff fields have concrete values and evidence references.
anchors.5: Handoff is implementation-ready, including constraints, unresolved decisions, and directly usable evidence.

dimensions.label: Scope discipline — stays in lane, no invented scope or out-of-skill work

anchors.1: Performs out-of-skill work or invents unsupported product rules.
anchors.2: Substantial adjacent-skill drift is present without a handoff.
anchors.3: Mostly in scope; one boundary is weakly handled.
anchors.4: Strictly in scope; adjacent work is named and handed off.
anchors.5: Boundaries improve the result: each adjacent concern is precisely deferred with the information needed to continue.

assertion_mapping.note: Map each scenario assertion to one or more scoring dimensions. A score of 1 indicates a material failure for its mapped assertion.

passing_threshold.note: A single candidate is competent at >=3 on every dimension and >=15/25; a paired release claim additionally requires the blind corpus thresholds.
